newsitem.title: UK: Atlantis says $200 mln optimum size for Asia fund.
newsitem.headline: Atlantis says $200 mln optimum size for Asia fund.

text.p: Britain's Atlantis Investment Management said on Friday an optimum size for its new Asian Growth Fund would be about $200 million.
In a statement announcing the launch of the fund, Atlantis said the initial offer period would end on May 30, with the first day of dealing on June 5.
It will be managed by former Schroders fund manager Tony Jordan and is incorporated in Luxembourg as a SICAV, or open-ended investment company.
The fund will invest in equity and equity related securities in Asia ex-Japan and to a lesser extent in Australia and New Zealand.
Atlantis said stock selection would drive asset allocation and as a result sector and country mix may be highly skewed. "Therefore performance is likely to differ markedly from the sector average."
Atlantis was set up in 1994 with a view to building specialist bottom-up funds run by established fund managers with a strong track record.
Jordan moved to Atlantis from Schroders in 1996. Atlantis chief executive officer Peter Irving was also at Schroders before founding Atlantis, which has assets under management of about $300 million.
Irving told Reuters early in May the fund was aiming to raise $50 million, but would be comfortable with a larger intake.
Atlantis has a policy of capping the size of a fund once it has reached a size above which stock selection will be hampered by liquidity considerations.

The Asian Growth fund will have the ability to invest in small and medium cap growth stocks, and will be well diversified, with typically 50 to 70 holdings. Diversification at country level will be achieved by limiting exposure to less liquid markets to 25 percent of assets.

In the initial portfolio, the stock pricking approach has resulted in a 25 percent weighting in Korea, and a zero weighting in Malaysia. Typical existing funds have about 15 to 20 percent in Malaysia.
The fund will also start with a 10 percent Thailand holding.
The fund is being marketed mostly in Europe, but will be available in other regions. It has also applied to the Securities and Investments Board to enable it to be offered to the retail market.
